ex.en: A security guard escorted us to the exit.
ex.zh: 一名警衛護送我們到出口。

ex.en: Please escort the visitors to the meeting room.
ex.zh: 請陪同訪客到會議室。

escort.en: to go with someone to protect or guide them

ex.en: The president arrived with a police escort.
ex.zh: 總統在警察護衛下抵達。

ex.en: Visitors must have an escort inside the factory.
ex.zh: 訪客在工廠內必須有人陪同。

escort.en: a person or group that goes with someone to protect them

ex.en: Where is the escalator?
ex.zh: 手扶梯在哪裡？

ex.en: When using the escalator, please hold the handrail and stand within the yellow line.
ex.zh: 搭乘手扶梯時，請握緊扶手，並站在黃線內。

ex.en: People who are not in a hurry stand on the right side of the escalator.
ex.zh: 不趕時間的人會站在手扶梯的右側。

escalator.en: a moving staircase that carries people up or down

ex.en: It is essentially a question of time.
ex.zh: 這基本上是時間的問題。

ex.en: The two plans are essentially the same.
ex.zh: 這兩個方案基本上是一樣的。

ex.en: Essentially, we need more staff.
ex.zh: 基本上，我們需要更多人手。

ex.en: That is the essence of the matter.
ex.zh: 這就是事情的本質。

ex.en: It's really unfortunate. You don't understand at all its essence.
ex.zh: 真可惜，你根本不懂它的精髓。

essence.en: the most important quality of something

ex.en: In essence, the two plans are the same.
ex.zh: 本質上，這兩個計畫是一樣的。

ex.en: In essence, we need more time.
ex.zh: 說穿了，我們需要更多時間。

ex.en: Add a few drops of vanilla essence.
ex.zh: 加幾滴香草精。

ex.en: This soap contains lemon essence.
ex.zh: 這塊肥皂含有檸檬精油。

essence.en: a strong liquid taken from a plant and used for flavor or smell

ex.en: By my estimation, the project will take six months.
ex.zh: 依我估計，這個專案需要六個月。

ex.en: Cost estimation is an important part of planning.
ex.zh: 成本估算是規劃中很重要的一環。

estimation.en: a rough guess of an amount or value

ex.en: In my estimation, he is the best candidate.
ex.zh: 依我看，他是最好的人選。

ex.en: She rose in her boss's estimation after the presentation.
ex.zh: 那次簡報後，老闆對她的評價提高了。

estimation.en: your opinion of someone or something

ex.en: Draft beer tastes especially good on a hot day.
ex.zh: 天氣熱的時候，生啤酒特別好喝。

ex.en: I like to listen to music, especially jazz.
ex.zh: 我喜歡聽音樂，尤其是爵士樂。

ex.en: The busses are especially crowded during rush hour.
ex.zh: 尖峰時段公車特別擁擠。

especially.en: more than usual or more than others

ex.en: That hotel was established about 50 years ago.
ex.zh: 那家飯店大約五十年前創立。

ex.en: The school was established in 1650.
ex.zh: 這所學校創立於 1650 年。

ex.en: People established churches and schools there.
ex.zh: 人們在那裡建立了教會和學校。

establish.en: to start something that will last

ex.en: We want to establish a long-term relationship with our clients.
ex.zh: 我們希望與客戶建立長期關係。

ex.en: It's important to establish clear rules.
ex.zh: 建立明確的規則很重要。

establish.en: to set up a relationship or rule

ex.en: Police are trying to establish the cause of the fire.
ex.zh: 警方正試圖查明起火原因。

ex.en: We need to establish the facts first.
ex.zh: 我們必須先查明事實。

establish.en: to find out or prove the facts

ex.en: Fruits and vegetables are essential to a balanced diet.
ex.zh: 蔬果是均衡飲食中不可或缺的。

ex.en: In the depths of winter, a hot-water bottle is essential.
ex.zh: 在寒冬裡，熱水袋是必備的。

ex.en: It is essential that every child have the same educational opportunities.
ex.zh: 讓每個孩子都享有相同的教育機會是非常重要的。

ex.en: Pack only the essentials for the trip.
ex.zh: 旅行只帶必需品就好。

ex.en: The course covers the essentials of accounting.
ex.zh: 這門課涵蓋會計的基本要點。

essential.en: the things you must have, or the most important points

ex.en: Each time he escaped, he returned to this region.
ex.zh: 他每次逃脫後都會回到這個地區。

ex.en: The cat escaped through the open window.
ex.zh: 貓從打開的窗戶溜走了。

escape.en: to get away from a place where you are kept

ex.en: They went to Edinburgh to escape from the summer heat.
ex.zh: 他們去愛丁堡避暑。

ex.en: I barely escaped being hit by the truck.
ex.zh: 我差點被卡車撞到。

ex.en: He looked for every possible means of escape.
ex.zh: 他尋找一切可能的逃脫方法。

ex.en: Reading is my escape from a stressful job.
ex.zh: 閱讀是我逃離工作壓力的方式。

escape.en: the act of getting away from a place or a bad situation

ex.en: She works in real estate.
ex.zh: 她從事房地產業。

ex.en: Real estate prices in Taipei are very high.
ex.zh: 台北的房價非常高。

ex.en: He left his entire estate to his daughter.
ex.zh: 他把全部遺產留給了女兒。

ex.en: The lawyer is handling her father's estate.
ex.zh: 律師正在處理她父親的遺產。

estate.en: all the money and things that a dead person leaves

ex.en: The family owns a large estate in the countryside.
ex.zh: 那個家族在鄉下擁有一大片莊園。

ex.en: The tea estate covers 200 hectares.
ex.zh: 這座茶園佔地 200 公頃。

estate.en: a large area of land with a big house, owned by one person

ex.en: It took me 2 hours to finish the essay.
ex.zh: 我花了兩個小時寫完這篇作文。

ex.en: When have we got to hand in our essays?
ex.zh: 我們什麼時候要交作文？

ex.en: All essays must be handed in on time.
ex.zh: 所有作文都必須準時繳交。

essay.en: a short piece of writing on one subject

ex.en: The establishment of the new branch took two years.
ex.zh: 新分公司的設立花了兩年。

ex.en: We celebrated the tenth anniversary of the company's establishment.
ex.zh: 我們慶祝公司成立十週年。

establishment.en: the act of starting something that will last

ex.en: The restaurant is a family-run establishment.
ex.zh: 這家餐廳是家族經營的店。

ex.en: Smoking is banned in all public establishments.
ex.zh: 所有公共場所都禁止吸菸。

establishment.en: a business or organization, such as a shop or restaurant

ex.en: He has been estranged from his brother for years.
ex.zh: 他和他哥哥已經好幾年不往來了。

ex.en: She contacted her estranged father after twenty years.
ex.zh: 她在二十年後聯絡了疏遠的父親。

estranged.en: no longer friendly or in contact with someone

ex.en: She is held in high esteem by her colleagues.
ex.zh: 她深受同事敬重。

ex.en: Praise from teachers can raise a child's self-esteem.
ex.zh: 老師的稱讚可以提升孩子的自尊心。

esteem.en: a feeling of respect and admiration

ex.en: The population of the country is roughly estimated at 50,000,000.
ex.zh: 這個國家的人口粗估約五千萬。

ex.en: The value of the painting was estimated at several million dollars.
ex.zh: 這幅畫估價數百萬元。

ex.en: The estimated delivery date is May 5.
ex.zh: 預計送達日期是 5 月 5 日。

ex.en: The buyer placed the deposit in escrow until the inspection was complete.
ex.zh: 買方將訂金交由第三方保管，直到檢查完成。

ex.en: The escrow account will release the funds after both parties sign.
ex.zh: 雙方簽署後，履約保管帳戶才會撥款。

escrow.en: money kept by a third person until a deal is completed

ex.en: If the customer is still unhappy, escalate the issue to your manager.
ex.zh: 如果客戶還是不滿意，就把問題上報給你的主管。

ex.en: The complaint was escalated to the head office.
ex.zh: 這起客訴被上報到總公司。

escalate.en: to pass a problem to a person with more authority

ex.en: The argument quickly escalated into a fight.
ex.zh: 爭吵很快演變成打架。

ex.en: Both sides want to stop the conflict from escalating.
ex.zh: 雙方都希望阻止衝突擴大。

escalate.en: to become much worse or more serious

ex.en: The population of the country is roughly estimated at 50,000,000.
ex.zh: 這個國家的人口粗略估計是五千萬左右。

ex.en: How much time do you estimate it'll take you to do that?
ex.zh: 你估計做那件事需要花費你多少時間呢？

ex.en: The value of the painting was estimated at several million dollars.
ex.zh: 這幅畫被估價數百萬元。

estimate.en: to guess an amount or value by roughly calculating it

ex.en: At a rough estimate, I would say the job will take two weeks.
ex.zh: 我想這工作粗略估計得花上兩個星期的時間。

ex.en: The builder gave us an estimate for the repairs.
ex.zh: 包商給了我們一份維修估價。

estimate.en: a rough guess of an amount, or a statement of the likely cost

ex.en: It is an established company with more than fifty years of history.
ex.zh: 這是一家有五十多年歷史的老公司。

ex.en: Smoking is an established cause of lung disease.
ex.zh: 吸菸是肺部疾病公認的成因。

ex.en: She is an established writer with many popular books.
ex.zh: 她是一位聲譽穩固的作家，有許多暢銷書。

essex.zh: 艾塞克斯郡（英格蘭郡名）

ex.en: Essex is a county in the east of England.
ex.zh: 艾塞克斯是英格蘭東部的一個郡。

ex.en: They live in a quiet village in Essex.
ex.zh: 他們住在艾塞克斯一個安靜的村莊。

ex.en: Many birds rest in the estuary where the river meets the sea.
ex.zh: 許多鳥類在河流入海的河口棲息。

ex.en: Fishermen sail out from the estuary at dawn.
ex.zh: 漁夫們在黎明時分從河口出海。

ex.en: Estrogen is a hormone that affects the female body.
ex.zh: 雌激素是一種影響女性身體的荷爾蒙。

ex.en: The doctor explained how estrogen levels change with age.
ex.zh: 醫生解釋了雌激素濃度如何隨年齡變化。

ex.en: The mayor espouses a green energy policy.
ex.zh: 市長支持綠能政策。

ex.en: Many young people espouse the idea of a simple life.
ex.zh: 許多年輕人信奉簡單生活的理念。

escalating.zh: 逐步升級；不斷擴大（escalate 的現在分詞）

ex.en: The escalating costs forced the team to cancel the project.
ex.zh: 不斷攀升的成本迫使團隊取消了這個計畫。

ex.en: Escalating tension between the two sides worried everyone.
ex.zh: 雙方不斷升高的緊張關係讓大家擔憂。

ex.en: The movie is a thriller about Cold War espionage.
ex.zh: 這部電影是關於冷戰時期間諜活動的驚悚片。

ex.en: He was accused of industrial espionage after leaving the firm.
ex.zh: 他離開公司後被指控從事商業間諜活動。

ex.en: He eschews fast food and cooks at home.
ex.zh: 他不吃速食，都在家煮。

ex.en: The politician eschewed negative advertising.
ex.zh: 這位政治人物避免使用負面廣告。

ex.en: Leaders worked to prevent an escalation of the conflict.
ex.zh: 領導人努力防止衝突升級。

ex.en: There has been an escalation in prices this year.
ex.zh: 今年物價持續上漲。

ex.en: I'll have a double espresso, please.
ex.zh: 請給我一杯雙份濃縮咖啡。

ex.en: He drinks an espresso every morning before work.
ex.zh: 他每天早上上班前都會喝一杯濃縮咖啡。

ex.en: Estonia is a small country in northern Europe.
ex.zh: 愛沙尼亞是北歐的一個小國。

ex.en: The capital of Estonia is Tallinn.
ex.zh: 愛沙尼亞的首都是塔林。

ex.en: The professor's lecture was too esoteric for most of the students.
ex.zh: 教授的課對大多數學生來說太深奧了。

ex.en: He collects esoteric books that few people have heard of.
ex.zh: 他收藏一些很少人聽過的冷門書籍。

ex.en: The essayist wrote about daily life in a small village.
ex.zh: 這位散文作家寫的是小村莊的日常生活。

ex.en: My favorite essayist publishes a new collection every year.
ex.zh: 我最喜歡的散文作家每年都會出版一本新文集。

esquire.zh: （置於姓名後的敬稱）先生；紳士

ex.en: The letter was addressed to John Smith, Esquire.
ex.zh: 這封信的收件人是約翰·史密斯先生。

ex.en: In the past, an esquire was a young man training to become a knight.
ex.zh: 過去，侍從是接受訓練、準備成為騎士的年輕人。

ex.en: She is an esteemed professor at the university.
ex.zh: 她是這所大學備受敬重的教授。

ex.en: Thank you, esteemed guests, for coming tonight.
ex.zh: 各位尊貴的來賓，謝謝你們今晚蒞臨。

ex.en: Food passes through the esophagus on its way to the stomach.
ex.zh: 食物在前往胃的途中會經過食道。

ex.en: The doctor looked inside her esophagus with a tiny camera.
ex.zh: 醫生用小攝影機檢查她的食道內部。

ex.en: The prisoner was caught escaping through a window.
ex.zh: 那名囚犯在從窗戶逃走時被抓到。

ex.en: We saw people escaping from the burning building.
ex.zh: 我們看到人們從著火的大樓裡逃出來。

ex.en: Gas was escaping from the broken pipe.
ex.zh: 瓦斯正從破裂的管子外洩。

ex.en: Steam kept escaping from the lid of the pot.
ex.zh: 蒸氣不斷從鍋蓋縫隙冒出來。

ex.en: This book is of especial interest to young readers.
ex.zh: 這本書特別能引起年輕讀者的興趣。

ex.en: Take especial care when handling the glass.
ex.zh: 搬動玻璃時要特別小心。

ex.en: The dog escaped through a hole in the fence.
ex.zh: 那隻狗從圍籬的洞逃走了。

ex.en: Two prisoners escaped last night.
ex.zh: 昨晚有兩名囚犯逃脫了。

ex.en: We narrowly escaped the heavy rain by running inside.
ex.zh: 我們跑進屋內，勉強躲過了大雨。

ex.en: He escaped serious injury in the accident.
ex.zh: 他在意外中沒有受到重傷。

ex.en: Years of estrangement kept the brothers apart.
ex.zh: 多年的疏遠讓兄弟倆各自分開。

ex.en: The argument led to an estrangement between the friends.
ex.zh: 那場爭吵造成朋友之間的隔閡。

ex.en: The building has great esthetic appeal.
ex.zh: 這棟建築有很高的美感。

ex.en: She chose the color for esthetic reasons, not practical ones.
ex.zh: 她出於美感而非實用的考量選了這個顏色。

escapade.zh: 冒險的惡作劇；越軌行為

ex.en: They laughed about their wild escapade from college days.
ex.zh: 他們笑談大學時代那次瘋狂的冒險。

ex.en: His latest escapade got him into trouble with the school.
ex.zh: 他最近的胡鬧讓他惹上了學校的麻煩。
